subject.title: [Feature]: Support custom HTTP headers on CLI WebSocket connections

question: Should OpenClaw add custom Gateway CLI WebSocket headers, and which credential-safe input sources should become the supported public contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but arbitrary headers affect reverse-proxy credentials, public CLI/config/env surface, and the gateway auth boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent product and security contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow secret-safe contract
options.body: Add header forwarding through approved sources only, with sanitizer, redaction, SecretInput/env handling where applicable, docs, and tests for WebSocket upgrade behavior.

options.title: Limit support to per-invocation headers
options.body: Support only a repeatable CLI flag first, avoiding durable config persistence while still allowing scripted operators to reach authenticated proxies.

options.title: Decline core CLI header support
options.body: Keep tunnels, Tailscale, VPNs, or proxy bypasses as the supported remote-management path and document that header-authenticating proxies remain outside the CLI contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow secret-safe contract
recommendation.body: Add header forwarding through approved sources only, with sanitizer, redaction, SecretInput/env handling where applicable, docs, and tests for WebSocket upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent mobile header implementations made the closest product/security decisions for the same authenticated-proxy deployment class.
